notes.text: Do not boot this packet under the live eebf8bb8. That host does not know the child field and treats the packet as a plain desktop run: no pdm1kbd, pdm1trackpadenum or pdm1trackpadchild, and no native sealed-writer FSM. The kernel would then load no PDM1SPIHID, the T1 collector would find no record (rc 1) and the supervisor would exit 1 before the compositor. That fails closed but outside the reviewed sealed mode, and proves nothing. Apply 0cf9ccc9 (my host review approves it for this packet) on root and M5, verify the hashes on both, and require before-start bootargs ending ' pdm1kbd=1 pdm1trackpadenum=1 pdm1trackpadchild=1'.

Several component status strings are freeze-time labels ('SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING', 'FROZEN_FOR_CLAUDE_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW', 'INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_PENDING'). The approvals are now in separate receipts (kernel source, SDK/KC recipe, registry gate, supervisor and addendum, host revision). The packet hashes do not depend on these labels.

Expected evidence under P1-P7, for the later qualifier, derived from source and not from my T1 ordering mistake: the DL15 chain (BEGIN, ENUM rc=0, ENDPOINT_WAIT, IDENTITY rc=0, SERVER_SOCKET, RECORDS, STATUS, RETURN, END); one DL16 gate export (11 chunks plus SHA-256) decoded by registry-gate-native/decode_records.py; the DL14 T1 record, whose descriptor must equal the 110-byte reference (gate note N1); and the unchanged DL12 observer lines. Wait cost comes from host file times. A live frame needs the source-derived cursor exclusion (supervisor note S1).
